Method: Derived from the GNU ld map in evidence/output.map.gz, parsed by cres_t4.service.linker_map.parse, cross-checked against `arm-none-eabi-ar t` over the archive itself. Versions and licences come from the BUILT TREE at the recorded commit -- MBEDTLS_VERSION_STRING from include/mbedtls/build_info.h, and the SPDX-License-Identifier from the three source files whose members actually shipped. No tool's bill of materials was consulted.
Matching: A candidate component matches when its name, lower-cased with punctuation removed, equals the entry's Name or any of its AcceptableNames. Anything else is a false positive; any unmatched entry is a false negative. Both are named individually.

Components.Name: Mbed TLS
Components.VersionNote: MBEDTLS_VERSION_STRING in include/mbedtls/build_info.h of the tree that was compiled, at commit 107ea89d (tag v3.6.2). Not inferred from a path or a filename.
Components.LicenceNote: Read from LICENSE in the built tree AND from the SPDX-License-Identifier header of aes.c, sha256.c and platform_util.c -- the three sources whose object members are in the image. This is the protocol's 'independently verified' bar: the licence of the code that shipped, not of the project in general. A tool reporting bare Apache-2.0 has dropped the user's choice of GPL-2.0-or-later; one reporting bare GPL-2.0 implies an obligation that does not apply.
Components.Uncertainty: THREE OF EIGHTY-SIX, AND THAT IS THE CASE. The component shipped, so Scope is 'shipped'. What did NOT ship is 83 of its object members -- every cipher but AES, every hash but SHA-256, the bignum and ASN.1 code, the error strings. A tool reporting 'Mbed TLS 3.6.2' is correct and says nothing about scope; a tool enumerating the archive's or the source tree's modules as components reports 86 things when 3 are in the image. Both are measured here, and the 83 names are listed rather than counted so a false claim can be named.

Components.Name: newlib
Components.VersionNote: The archive paths carry GCC's version (12.2.1), not newlib's own, and the toolchain package manifest was not captured. Establishing it needs `dpkg -s libnewlib-arm-none-eabi` from the build container, which the recipe should capture and does not yet.
Components.LicenceNote: newlib is a COLLECTION under several licences -- BSD variants plus historical terms on individual files -- and naming one would be wrong. A real answer needs COPYING.NEWLIB, which is in the toolchain package rather than this tree.

Evidence.Note: crt0.o is counted here because it comes from the newlib install (arm-none-eabi/lib/thumb/v7-m/nofp/crt0.o), not from GCC's own directory.

Components.Uncertainty: THE LARGEST THING IN THE IMAGE AT 43KB OF 58KB, which is worth knowing before anybody describes this firmware as 'mostly Mbed TLS'. The C library is in every build and almost no bill of materials lists it. Counting libnosys.a with newlib is a judgement -- the semihosting stubs ship inside the same toolchain package -- and AcceptableNames admits either name so a tool reporting them separately does not register as a false positive.

Components.Name: GCC runtime startup
Components.VersionNote: Read from the objects' own path (/usr/lib/gcc/arm-none-eabi/12.2.1/thumb/v7-m/nofp/), which is the compiler's version. Heuristic rather than pinned because a filesystem layout is not a manifest.
Components.LicenceNote: GCC's published runtime terms. The runtime exception is the part that matters to a device maker and the part most tools drop.

Evidence.Note: No libgcc.a member was pulled into this build: nothing here needs the integer division helpers that pulled it into case 001.

Components.Uncertainty: 425 bytes of C++-style static initialisation and frame setup that nothing in the source mentions and every image contains. Reported as its own component rather than folded into newlib because the objects come from GCC's directory, not newlib's -- a distinction visible only in the map.

NotComponents.Name: the application
NotComponents.Why: First-party code -- app.c, which calls SHA-256 and AES and nothing else. One object, 252 bytes. A tool reporting it as a third-party component is producing a false positive.

NotComponents.Name: *crtend?.o
NotComponents.Why: NOT AN OBJECT FILE. A linker-script wildcard that the map prints with zero bytes. It is recorded here so nobody mistakes it for a discarded component, and so a parser that reports it as one can be seen to be wrong.

Open.Question: Does the total reconcile?
Open.Detail: 14284 + 43330 + 425 = 58039 across the three components, plus 252 of first-party code = 58291, which is the map's own LinkedBytes. It reconciles exactly.

Open.Question: Should the 83 unpulled members make Mbed TLS a partial component?
Open.Detail: The protocol has no vocabulary for 'this component shipped, at 3.5% of its code'. CycloneDX has no field for it either. The honest reporting is the component plus the evidence, which is what this case records -- but a device maker asked 'are you affected by a bignum CVE' wants the answer 'that code is not in the image', and no standard format carries it. This is the strongest argument for the evidence-per-component card.
